body: The 2027 BRIT Awards trophy has been designed by former Turner Prize-winning visual artist Dame Rachel Whiteread (Nov. 27). Each year a different designer shapes a distinct creative vision for their trophy, modeled on the image of Britannia, traditionally represented by a female warrior with a shield and helmet. In recent years, the trophy has been designed by iconic names such as Dame Vivienne Westwood, Sir Peter Blake, Tracey Emin, Dame Zaha Hadid, and last year’s designer, Matthew Williamson. Whiteread took on 2027’s assignment, and her trophy will be presented to winners at the ceremony on Feb. 27 at the Co-op Live in Manchester. In 1993, Whiteread became the first woman to win the Turner Prize, an accolade presented annually to a British visual artist; previous victors include Damien Hirst, Gilbert & George, and Anish Kapoor. Four years after her win, in 1997, she was the first woman to represent Britain at the Venice Biennale. Her work primarily focuses on casting, and her Turner Prize-winning exhibit House (1993) featured a life-sized concrete cast of a Victorian terraced house in east London. title: Android just had one of its worst quarters, and Apple is benefiting
summary: Android just recorded its lowest-ever share for a third quarter, with Apple's iOS bucking the trend.
body: TL;DR Android accounted for 74% of global smartphone sales in Q3 2026, down five points from a year ago and its lowest-ever share for a third quarter, per Counterpoint Research. iOS climbed to a record Q3 share of 21% as iPhone sales grew year-on-year, even as the overall market shrank 16%. HarmonyOS held at 5% globally and took 22% of China’s market, with HUAWEI growing 12% while China’s market shrank 10%. The memory shortage has been dragging down phone sales all year, and new data shows it may be hurting Android more than its rivals. According to Counterpoint Research , global smartphone sales fell 16% year-on-year in Q3 2026, a sharper drop than the 11% decline seen in Q2. Android’s share of those sales slipped to 74%, down from 79% in Q3 2025. That’s the lowest share Android has ever posted in a third quarter, though it’s still a touch above the 72% it hit in Q4 2025, when new iPhones typically give Apple a seasonal bump.
